chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, who said: Yaqub ibn Yazid and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to me, from Hammad ibn Isa, from someone he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Blood-letting (Hijamah) on Monday from the latter part of the day removes the disease completely from the body.

key_terms.آخِرِ النَّهَارِ: The latter part of the day / afternoon

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended time and day for blood-letting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, the virtue of Hijamah (blood-letting) is specifically highlighted for Monday during the late afternoon, a time traditionally associated with the dissipation of bodily humors. This practice is presented not merely as a medical remedy but as a Sunnah-based prophetic tradition that effectively removes disease from the body entirely, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating spiritual and physical well-being through the Imams' guidance.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-66 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Yaqoob ibn Yazid and Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil-Khat’tab, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa, on the authority of someone who had narrated that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“It was the Prophet (MGB)’s custom was to have blood-letting done for him on Monday afternoons. He (MGB) used to say, ‘Having phlebotomy done on Monday afternoons would immediately relieves one’s pains.’”
